newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Nordic airline to axe Stockholm-Brussels service.
newsitem.headline: Nordic airline to axe Stockholm-Brussels service.

text.p: Nordic European Airlines said it will end in December its recently-started service between Stockholm and Brussels because Swedish civil servants did not support the special cut-price flights.

Managing director Carl-Johan Stahle said that under an agreement with the Swedish government, Nordic European would charge up to 30 percent less than the prevailing rate, in return for at least 550 return bookings per week.
"So far we have hardly got 10 percent of that - only between 30 and 50 passengers a week from the state," Stahle told Swedish Radio. "Our last flight will be on December 1."
Stahle said he will however meet government officials on Tuesday to discuss the possibility of financial guarantees to resume the service which began in mid-October.
Claes Sonnerby of state audit office RRV which initiated scheme said government departments were encouraged but not obliged to take advantage of the cheaper flights.
Swedish politicians and civil servants make about 10,000 return trips between Stockholm and Brussels every year, and the Nordic scheme would save the state an estimated 40 million crowns.
The Nordic service leaves Stockholm early and returns from Brussels the same evening.

But many travellers apparently preferred to travel to Brussels the night before their meetings, thus earning daily allowance. In addition, other airlines including Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) either lowered rates or were seen as more attractive because of bonus points, Swedish news agency TT reported.
